results.title: Lifetime experience
results.text: This was my second time in Pashupatinath; even more emotional than the first one as this time I got to watch a Hindu cremation ceremony from the very start to the end, taking place on the ghats located on the banks of Bagmati River. You cannnot say that you have visited Kathmandu unless you have not visited Pashupatinath. This is a unique experience as one could see life, death, hope, despair all in the same shot. However, the smell and smoke might be disturbing for some people so you can bring some wet wipes or scarf to avoid this.Entrance to the main temple at Pashupatinath is forbidden for the Non-Hindus but still you can take a glimpse of the Nandi bull.

results.title: The Vatican of Hindus!
results.text:
Sadhus, Holiest Hindu Temple, Cremation - all the "holy' gathered in one square - we were amazed. 

As our family have Christian and Muslim background, teaching the kids our other faith is part of our parenting philosophy. The search for knowledge and truth for the kids actually got sparked in this place. 

Lots of ideas, lots of questions, lots of rituals.

We were also able to visit the elderly house just besides the crematoria place. It was a good lesson on life, death and making each day counts. 

A holy and spiritual day for a non- Hindu family.

results.title: Pashupatinath Temple Kathmandu Nepal
results.text:
Pashupatinath Temple Kathmandu (Nepal) is one of the most significant Hindu temples of Shiva in the world, located on the banks of the Bagmati River in the eastern part of Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal dedicated to Lord Shiva. Pashupathinath is the guardian spirit and the holiest of all Shiva shrines in Nepal. In the sanctum of the temple, there is a very attractive, about three feet high Shivalinga with four faces.These faces are also defined as the symbol of four dharmas and four Vedas. Pashupatinath Temple is regarded as one of the most important places of pilgrimages for the followers of Hinduism.Thousands of devotees from within and outside the country come to pay homage to Pashupatinath every day. Pashupatinath temple is the biggest and most visited temple of lord shiva in the world.
According to legends, the Pandavas sought the blessings of lord Shiva to atone their sin after the battle of Mahabharata. Lord Shiva eluded them repeatedly and while fleeing took refuge at Kedarnath in the form of a bull. On being followed, he dived into ground leaving behind his hump on the surface and appeared in Nepal as Pashupatinath.

results.title: wonderful ancient temple
results.text:
It is an ancient temple having mythological and historical value for all Hindus.  Lord Shiva is known as Lord Pashupathinath here, because the shape of Linga is the head of sacred cow.  All the four sides of Linga are having different faces.  Only Hindus are allowed inside the temple and photography is strictly prohibited.  The Temple is situate on the banks of river Bagmati.
If you are in Nepal, this is the first place to visit.  Do not buy any rudrakshis as suggested by your tour operators or guides from the local shops.  Most of them are fake and do not take risk of wasting money.

results.title: pashupatinath
results.text: Very moving experience.  We saw several funerals taking place with bodies being cremated by the side of the river.  Also were introduced to real Sadhus living by the temple.  Very emotional visit highly recommend

results.title: Amazing ritual
results.text: So yes, we saw them burning their dead. We saw them bathing in the filthy river searching for coins or whatever leftovers from the dead. We barely missed animal sacrifices in a temple, but could still find ourselves inside a blood-drawn circle. We also saw a paralysed monkey that had tried to play with the electric cables. It was all disturbing. So many questions and self-wondering coming in bursts and we were incapable of reacting and of understanding. Another culture, another world.

results.title: Hire a guide for a an hour
results.text: A guide will provide you much insight into the practices of the cremations and won't cost you much (about 10$. And do stop to take pictures of the sadhu and leave them a tip. (even though they are fake).

results.title: What an amazing place
results.text: I saw this once on tv but nothing compares to seeing it in real life. We spent two hours there in the company of a guide which is essential to really understand what's is happening around you. We saw funeral pyres, sadhu religious men and lots more. Do visit if you are in Kathmandu!!

results.title: A glimpse of spiritual life
results.text: An amazing spiritual centre for Hindus, pilgrims and ordinary folk alike. Sit by the banks of the river and watch life unfold - a procession carrying the dead, the rituals, the cremation; on the other side, you can see people eating, praying, etc. Then walk up the hill and watch monkeys dart in and out of trees; the braver ones will come near you but they don't attack (unless you hv something edible in your hands). and Please note that the govt recently started to charge tourists an entry fee to visit the temple complex, but it's worth it.

results.title: Well organised to handle huge crowds
results.text: Pasupatinath at first sight looks no different from any other temple in Kathmandu but once you are in, you find the mighty Nandi and the imposing temple complex. There is so much to it that one can spend hours even if one is not offering the puja. The cows loitering and the flocks of pigeons too lend grace to the place. Foreigners can be seen clicking pics from the other side. Though photography is restricted inside one can still come back with few memories from the area around the main temple. The shoe stand is well organised and there are few priests to disturb. I found the viewing gallery in front of the main temple to be of great benefit.

results.title: Long way for nothing
results.text: It was a long bumpy trip to get here. It was very dirty and not inspiring. There are better ways to spend your time in Kathmandu

results.title: Pashupatinath Hindu Temple
results.text:
Pashupatinath is believed to be one of the biggest Hindus temple of Shiva, It is regarded as most sacred among the Temples of Lord Shiva. Only Hindus believers are allowed to enter the Temple Premises. Non Hindu Visitors are allowed to have a look at the Temples from other bank of Bagmati River. This Temple has gold pinnacle Pagoda style architecture has four main doors, all covered with silver sheets and two level roofs are of coppers with gold covering. 

There is a statue of large bull near to the western door which is also cover in gold. There is a small river by the side of the Temple which is believed as Holy River, Hindus believe that they will go into the Heaven if they cremate into the bank of this river. So there will be many cremations going every day. So all these made very interesting place to visit in Kathmandu valley.

results.title: A Place of Fascination and Contemplation
results.text: Death is part of life. At this most holy of Hindu temples bodies are prepared and cremated in the open and death can be experienced in life.  In the west death is hidden, discrete, outsourced to professionals. For a temple that deals with death it is, as others have remarked, a peaceful place, yet one full of life, mystery and evidence of a rich culture. It is a one stop shop for everything - shaved heads, the right robes, the wood, the accelerant, etc. everything is available there. Non Hindus cannot go into the temple at the centre of the complex, although you can stand at the entrance and look in. Otherwise you are free to wander, and wonder. It will most likely be an experience you will never forget. I have visited this place many times when we have visitors and for my own interest. A place of fascination and contemplation.

results.title: Didn't go in; objected to the stiff entry fee.
results.text: Trying to turn a temple into Disneyland.  Shopping all around; many people dressed as holy men who then want to charge to have you take their photos.  Made me doubt their authenticity.  We walked all around the outside, which was not very impressive.

results.title: Too pricey for how dirty it is
results.text: It is very interesting as you can see the cremations, but considering the price for the entrance, the place is almost ruined down and dirty.

results.title: Serene !
results.text: An important temple for Hindu's. Full of stories and anecdotes. Great place to meditate. You can pick up some antiques at a great price near this temple if you are really good at bargaining.
